subject.title: [Feature]: First-class multi-instance management for Docker installs

question: Should OpenClaw core own first-class Docker instance create/list/delete/update commands, or should multi-instance Docker remain documented manual Compose/profile operation for now?
rationale: The requested work creates official operator UX and lifecycle state across Docker, config/state/workspace roots, ports, Compose naming, update, deletion, and isolation/security contracts; that is a product boundary decision rather than a narrow bug repair.

options.title: Sponsor core Docker lifecycle
options.body: Approve a minimal core design for named Docker instances with explicit identity, ports, persistence, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts before implementation.

options.title: Keep manual primitives
options.body: Leave the current profile, env, Docker Compose, setup script, and ClawDock helpers as the supported path while tracking this as design backlog.

options.title: Route to external wrapper
options.body: Decline core ownership unless a missing core API is identified, and ask contributors to maintain a wrapper or ClawHub package around current primitives.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core Docker lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve a minimal core design for named Docker instances with explicit identity, ports, persistence, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible history across Docker setup/docs, gateway lifecycle, and the product-level guardrails this decision needs.
